name: Brian Chesky
notes: LIST MEMBERSHIP CONFIRMED: ycombinator.com/companies/airbnb names him -- "Brian Chesky is the co-founder, Head of Community, and CEO of Airbnb, which he started with Joe Gebbia and Nathan Blecharczyk in 2008." The Obama O's / Cap'n McCain's cereal boxes (2008) were a fundraising stunt for AirBed & Breakfast, not a separate company (Wikipedia Chesky: "They developed and designed election-themed cereal boxes to generate funds."). Pre-Airbnb employment is industrial design at 3DID in Los Angeles after the 2004 RISD graduation (Wikipedia: "Chesky moved to Los Angeles following graduation from RISD to work for 3DID as an industrial designer."), which is not software/internet. The hit entity is therefore Airbnb, his first founded company. rev10 BOUNDED 2008-2015, span 7 years, both ends sourced -- FALLBACK BARRED. Airbnb IPO'd in 2020 but revenue is documented from 2015 (S-1), so the IPO fallback is barred. LOWER END: the frame's founding-year rule. YC company page: "Founded: 2008"; Wikipedia Airbnb: "The site Airbedandbreakfast.com was launched on August 11, 2008." A company cannot earn before it exists. Corroborating below-bar figure: Inc. (2014 Company of the Year, archived at https://web.archive.org/web/20210309113404/https://www.inc.com/magazine/201412/burt-helm/airbnb-company-of-the-year-2014.html): "once Obama-mania left Denver, their revenue (a 6 to 12 percent cut of each rental, same as they charge today) puttered along at about $200 a week" -- $200/week annualised is ~$10,400 against the 2008 rev10 bar. python3 -m src.cpi 2008 output: revenue year 2008, thresholds in nominal USD: rev10 ($10,000,000 constant 2026) = $6,687,612. UPPER END: Airbnb S-1 (filed 16 Nov 2020) selected financials, years ended December 31, "2015 2016 2017 2018 2019" / "Revenue $ 919,041 $ 1,655,576 $ 2,561,721 $ 3,651,985 $ 4,805,239" (in thousands). 2015 revenue is $919.041 million. python3 -m src.cpi 2015 output: revenue year 2015, thresholds in nominal USD: rev10 ($10,000,000 constant 2026) = $7,362,080. $919.041M is 125x the 2015 bar. The exact crossing year inside 2008-2015 is not published: Wikipedia's finances table lists 2014 as $0.4bn but cites no primary filing; Business Insider (9 Mar 2012) estimated GMV not company revenue ("Airbnb booked approximately $52.8 million last year") and those estimates are not used. a1: born 29 August 1981, Niskayuna, New York (Wikipedia Chesky: "Brian Joseph Chesky (born August 29, 1981)"). a2: BFA Industrial Design, RISD, 2004 -- RISD's own 19 May 2017 commencement release: "Originally from New York, he earned a BFA in Industrial Design from RISD in 2004" and styles him "Brian Chesky (RISD '04 Industrial Design)". Last credential completed; no graduate degree. a3: JUDGMENT CALL -- set equal to a4 (2008) under the Blakely convention that founding counts as first domain work when no prior domain employment exists. 3DID (2004) was industrial design of toys, guitars and a toilet seat, not software/internet/hospitality-marketplace work. a4 2008: YC founder bio as quoted above. a6: 10 December 2020 IPO (Wikipedia Airbnb: "On December 10, 2020, Airbnb became a public company via an initial public offering, raising $3.5 billion on Nasdaq.").

name: Phil Knight
notes: LIST MEMBERSHIP CONFIRMED: forbes.com/profile/phil-knight/ names him -- "Phil Knight, cofounder of shoe giant Nike, retired as chairman in 2016 after 52 years at the company." Personal Stats: "Source of Wealth Nike, Self Made", Self-Made Score 8. SERIAL-FOUNDER CHECK -- NO EARLIER VENTURE FOUND. Pre-BRS work is salaried CPA (Coopers & Lybrand then Price Waterhouse) and teaching at Portland State, neither of which is footwear. The hit entity is Blue Ribbon Sports, founded with Bill Bowerman and later renamed Nike; Laika is decades later. rev10 BOUNDED 1970-1972, span 2 years, both ends sourced -- FALLBACK BARRED. Nike IPO'd in December 1980 but revenue is documented from the 1960s, so the IPO fallback is barred. LOWER END (below-bar year 1969): FundingUniverse / International Directory of Company Histories: "By the end of the decade, Knight's venture had expanded to include several stores and 20 employees and sales were nearing $300,000." python3 -m src.cpi 1969 output: revenue year 1969, thresholds in nominal USD: rev10 ($10,000,000 constant 2026) = $1,139,953. $300,000 is 26% of the 1969 bar. Corroboration that 1969 is still below even on a higher figure: Britannica, "by 1969 Blue Ribbon Sports had sold $1 million worth of shoes" -- $1.0M is 88% of the same 1969 bar, still short. UPPER END (above-bar year 1972): FundingUniverse: "In their first year of distribution, the company's new products grossed $1.96 million" -- the paragraph places this the year after the 1971 Swoosh/Nike-brand introduction and the 1972 U.S. Olympic Trials promotion. python3 -m src.cpi 1972 output: revenue year 1972, thresholds in nominal USD: rev10 ($10,000,000 constant 2026) = $1,298,366. $1.96M is 151% of the 1972 bar (51% clear; not inside the 20% caution band). No sourced 1970 or 1971 company-wide figure, so the crossing is bounded 1970-1972 rather than pinned. 1964 first-year sales of $8,000 (same source: "BRS sold 1,300 pairs of Japanese running shoes in 1964, its first year, to gross $8,000") are far below the 1964 bar of $962,903 but are not needed once 1969 is sourced below. a1: born 24 February 1938, Portland, Oregon (Wikipedia: "Philip Hampson Knight (born February 24, 1938)"). a2: Stanford MBA 1962 is the last credential completed -- Wikipedia: "He graduated with a master's degree in business administration from Stanford in 1962." Prior: University of Oregon BBA 1959 (same article). a3 1963: first paid work in footwear -- FundingUniverse: "At the end of 1963, Knight's arrangements in Japan came to fruition when he took delivery of 200 pairs of Tiger athletic shoes, which he stored in his father's basement and peddled at various track meets in the area." Accounting is not this bucket's domain. a4 1964: Forbes profile: "In 1964, they each put up $500 to start Blue Ribbon Sports." Wikipedia agrees the Bowerman handshake on 25 January 1964 is "the birth date of Blue Ribbon Sports". FU's 1962 key-date ("Philip H. Knight founds Blue Ribbon Sports") is the invented trading name for the Onitsuka meeting, not the partnership; 1964 is used. a6: December 1980 IPO -- FundingUniverse: "In December 1980, Nike went public, offering two million shares of stock."

name: François Pinault
notes: LIST MEMBERSHIP CONFIRMED: forbes.com/profile/francois-pinault/ names him -- "François Pinault is honorary chairman of luxury group Kering, which owns fashion brands Saint Laurent, Alexander McQueen and Gucci." Source of Wealth "Luxury goods, Self Made"; "Pinault founded Kering, which started as a wood and building materials company, in 1963." EXCLUDED under the revised frame; the 1988 Paris listing cannot date the hit, because an earlier crossing is known to have occurred. SERIAL-FOUNDER CHECK: the hit entity is the continuous timber-then-retail firm he founded (Établissements François Pinault / Pinault SA / PPR / Kering), not a later luxury acquisition. Gucci 1999 is decades after the timber business was already large. FALLBACK BARRED. Wikipedia: "On 25 October 1988, Pinault SA was taken public in the Paris stock exchange". Quartr (19 Dec 2024, https://quartr.com/insights/edge/house-of-pinault-the-history-and-business-of-kering-and-gucci): "By then, it owned 180 companies with an annual turnover of 10 billion francs (approximately $7 billion)." CURRENCY CONVERSION: 10.0bn FRF ÷ 5.96 (1988 avg, MeasuringWorth France official rate 5.96 FRF per USD) = US$1.68bn, against the 1988 rev10 bar. python3 -m src.cpi 1988 output: revenue year 1988, thresholds in nominal USD: rev10 ($10,000,000 constant 2026) = $3,674,564. $1.68bn is ~457x the bar, so 1988 is far above -- and therefore later than the truth. (Quartr's parenthetical "~$7 billion" uses a later conversion and is not used.) WHY THE CROSSING CANNOT BE BOUNDED: the sourced founding year is a valid lower end (frame.md), but the first published above-bar revenue figure is 1988, 26 years later, which exceeds the 10-year span. Attempts for an intervening figure: (1) L'Express 10 Dec 1998 timeline, "Mars 1973: il vend 80% du capital de Pinault Distribution (60 salariés) pour 30 millions de francs à un groupe britannique, Venesta, soit dix fois le cash-flow" -- that is an equity-sale price and a cash-flow multiple, NOT annual revenue, so it cannot be compared to the bar (converting 30m FRF at 4.45 FRF/USD 1973 avg would be an inference even as a valuation). (2) Guardian 3 Apr 1999 repeats the same 1973 Venesta sale ("for 10 times cashflow - a handy 30 million francs") with no CA. (3) French Wikipedia, Les Echos 1991 and 1995, and Le Figaro 15 Sep 2023 were searched for 1960s-1970s chiffre d'affaires; none names an annual revenue figure for any year before 1988. The 1962 founding therefore cannot serve as one end of a legal bound. Window 1962-1988 is not a sourced bound, so the row is excluded rather than dated. python3 -m src.cpi 1962 output: revenue year 1962, thresholds in nominal USD: rev10 ($10,000,000 constant 2026) = $938,054. a1: born 21 August 1936, Les Champs-Géraux (Wikipedia). a2 UNKNOWN: last credential actually COMPLETED is not sourced. Guardian: "Pinault left the College Saint-Martin in Rennes at 16 without a qualification to his name." Forbes Personal Stats: "Education Drop Out, High School." Journal du Net: "a quitté le collège Saint Martin à Rennes à l'âge de 16 ans, sans même avoir le bac." The year he left (1952) is the dropout year, not a completed credential, and no brevet/certificat d'études year was found after two attempts (Wikipedia/Guardian/Forbes and the Gallimard biography excerpt). a3 1952: first paid timber work at his father's sawmill -- Gallimard excerpt of Jean Bothorel, François Pinault: une enfance bretonne: "C'est donc sans regret qu'en 1952, à la demande de son père qui a besoin de lui à la scierie, François Pinault reprend le chemin de la ferme familiale. Il a alors 16 ans." Timber is the domain the hit came from. a4 1962: his own words in Paris Match (24 Oct 2013): "j'ai acheté, en 1962, un petit terrain dans la zone industrielle de Rennes pour monter un négoce de bois. J'ai fondé Les Etablissements François Pinault, sur la route de Lorient." L'Express timeline agrees ("1962: il quitte la petite scierie de Trévérien ... pour monter sa propre affaire"). Wikipedia and Forbes say 1963; the founder's own dated sentence is used. Not an inherited going concern: he sold the family mill after his father's death and started a new trading firm with a borrowed 100,000 francs (Guardian). a6: 1988 IPO, recorded as the later scale marker, not as the hit.

name: Todd Graves
notes: LIST MEMBERSHIP CONFIRMED: forbes.com/profile/todd-graves/ names him -- "Todd Graves founded fried chicken finger fast-food chain Raising Cane's." Self-Made Score 8; "He launched Raising Cane's in 1996, using his savings and an SBA loan." SERIAL-FOUNDER CHECK -- NO EARLIER VENTURE FOUND. Pre-Cane's work is salaried (oil-refinery boilermaker, Alaska sockeye fishing) plus undated college restaurant jobs at UGA; Cane's is his first founded company. EXCLUDED. FALLBACK BARRED: the company never IPO'd, and an earlier crossing is known because 2011-2012 revenue is far above the bar. Dallas Morning News, 19 May 2012: "Annual sales: $250 million projected for 2012, up 25 percent from 2011" and "will produce $250 million in revenue this year". python3 -m src.cpi 2012 output: revenue year 2012, thresholds in nominal USD: rev10 ($10,000,000 constant 2026) = $7,131,511. $250M is 35x the 2012 bar. python3 -m src.cpi 2011 output: revenue year 2011, thresholds in nominal USD: rev10 ($10,000,000 constant 2026) = $6,986,920. Implied 2011 sales of $200M ($250M / 1.25) is 29x the 2011 bar. WHY THE CROSSING CANNOT BE BOUNDED: founding year is a valid lower end. Dallas Morning News: "Founded: Aug. 26, 1996, Baton Rouge, La." and "We made a $30 profit the first month" (profit, not revenue, but the company cannot earn before it exists). python3 -m src.cpi 1996 output: revenue year 1996, thresholds in nominal USD: rev10 ($10,000,000 constant 2026) = $4,873,534. The first sourced above-bar annual-revenue figure is 2011/2012, 15-16 years after founding, which exceeds the 10-year span. Two further attempts for an intervening figure: (1) CNBC 5 Oct 2024 / Dallas News both give Hurricane Katrina 2005 as "21 of his 28 locations" down, a store COUNT not a dollar figure; (2) SCORE.org 2010 100th-restaurant story and NRN 26 Sep 2024 ("Things started to really accelerate around 2011, when the company opened its 100th restaurant") likewise give unit counts, not revenue. No 1996-2006 annual sales figure was found. Window 1996-2011 is not a sourced bound, so the row is excluded rather than dated. Do NOT report 2012 as the hit year -- that would date the career 15 years late. a1: born 1972 (Wikipedia infobox "Todd Bartlett Graves 1972"; Dallas News 19 May 2012 gives age 40, consistent). a2: last credential completed is University of Georgia BA, telecommunications, 1994 -- Dallas News AT A GLANCE: "Education: Degree in telecommunications, University of Georgia, 1994." a3 JUDGMENT CALL: set equal to a4 (1996). He worked "at a lot of different restaurants and bars" while at UGA (How I Built This transcript) but no source dates those jobs to a year; the first dated paid work in foodservice is opening Cane's. a4 1996: Dallas News as quoted. a6: Nation's Restaurant News 26 Sep 2024, citing Technomic, "Raising Cane's ended 2019 with $1.46 billion in sales and 457 locations" -- a later scale marker, not the crossing.

name: Ernest Garcia II
notes: LIST MEMBERSHIP CONFIRMED: forbes.com/profile/ernest-garcia-ii/ names him -- "Ernest Garcia, II is the biggest shareholder of Carvana, an online platform for selling used cars and making auto loans that conducted an IPO in 2017." Self-Made Score 9; Source of Wealth "Used cars, Self Made". SERIAL-FOUNDER CHECK -- THE HIT IS NOT CARVANA. Carvana was founded in 2012 by his son Ernest Garcia III as a DriveTime subsidiary and spun out; Garcia II is a shareholder, not its founder. His first auto venture is Ugly Duckling / DriveTime. An earlier real-estate development firm (Lincoln S&L related, bankrupt ~1990) predates Duck Ventures; no revenue figure for it was found after two attempts (Wikipedia, Reference for Business), so it is not treated as a prior crossing. INHERITED-GOING-CONCERN CHECK: Ugly Duckling Rent-A-Car was founded 1977 by Thomas S. Duck, Sr., reached $65 million sales in 1985, and declared bankruptcy in 1989. Garcia bought the ASSETS of that bankrupt rental firm in 1990 and in 1992 pivoted to used-car sales under the Ugly Duckling name. The 1977 founding year is therefore barred as a lower bound (frame.md inherited-going-concern rule). The relevant entity for the crossing is the used-car/finance business he started in 1992. rev10 BOUNDED 1992-1995, span 3 years, both ends sourced -- FALLBACK BARRED. The 1996 NASDAQ IPO cannot date the hit because 1995 revenue is documented. LOWER END: Reference for Business (International Directory of Company Histories): "He started out by buying a small used-car dealership in Phoenix and later in 1992 purchased a second dealership in Tucson." A company cannot earn used-car revenue before that dealership exists. UPPER END: same source, "At the end of 1995, after four years in business, ... total revenues, the bulk of which were comprised by used car sales, had consistently increased, reaching $58.2 million revenues ($47.8 million from car sales alone) at the end of 1995." python3 -m src.cpi 1995 output: revenue year 1995, thresholds in nominal USD: rev10 ($10,000,000 constant 2026) = $4,733,757. $58.2M is 12.3x the 1995 bar. Corroboration of the above-bar side: "Total 1996 revenues increased almost 30 percent to $75.6 million." python3 -m src.cpi 1996 output: revenue year 1996, thresholds in nominal USD: rev10 ($10,000,000 constant 2026) = $4,873,534. No sourced 1993 or 1994 company-wide figure, so the crossing is bounded rather than pinned. a1: born 1 May 1957 (Wikipedia: "Ernest García II was born May 1, 1957"). a2 UNKNOWN: Forbes profile says "Education: Drop Out, University of Arizona" and "Garcia II dropped out of school before graduating to become a stockbroker"; Wikipedia says "He dropped out, but eventually earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Arizona" (citing the 2017 Forbes feature). The two conflict on whether a BA was completed, and neither gives a year, so the last completed credential is not dated. a3 1992: first paid work in used-car retail -- the Phoenix dealership, same source as a5 lower end. Pre-1992 work is real estate, banking and securities, which is not this bucket's domain. a4 1990: "In 1990 he formed a company called Duck Ventures, Inc., which purchased the assets of Ugly Duckling Rent-A-Car." Wikipedia instead dates the Ugly Duckling purchase to 1991; 1990 is used as the first dated entity he founded. a6: Carvana IPO 2017 -- Forbes profile: "an online platform for selling used cars and making auto loans that conducted an IPO in 2017." That is a later scale marker of the family auto group, not the first hit.
